questions.explanation: D — “do not adapt,” broadly. Peripheral chemoreceptors retain hypoxic responsiveness, unlike central CO₂ response adaptation; A/B are not the best contrast, C/E false. Key imprecise: peripheral responses can change with acclimatization and are not literally non-adapting.
questions.sourceQuestion: Peripheral Chemoreceptors:

questions.question: Peripheral chemoreceptors:
options: Are always exposed to arterial blood
Respond to changes in CO2 rather than to O2
Respond to changes in H+ rather than O2
Their afferent nerve fibers pass through the trigeminal nerve to the respiratory center
questions.explanation: A — exposed to arterial blood. Carotid and aortic bodies sample arterial blood; B/E are false, while C/D misstate relative sensitivity.
questions.sourceQuestion: Peripheral chemoreceptors:

questions.question: A person with a cervical rib, complained of pain and tingling down his arms, this is due to the compression of which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: A (T1 spinal nerve) — Cervical ribs can compress the lower brachial plexus/T1 root; phrenic (B), intercostal (C), vagus (D), and brachiocephalic vein (E) are not the characteristic structures.
questions.sourceQuestion: A person with a cervical rib, complained of pain and tingling down his arms, this is due to the compression of which of the following structures? (repeated)

questions.question: A 32-year-old woman sustained a chest injury during a car crash. Upon admission, a physical examination revealed profuse swelling, inflammation, and deformation of the chest wall. An X-ray revealed an uncommon fracture of the manubrium at the manubriosternal joint. Which of the following is the most likely to be involved in such an injury?
questions.explanation: E (2nd rib) — The sternal angle/manubriosternal junction marks the 2nd costal cartilage; ribs 1, 4, 5, and 7 attach elsewhere.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 32-year-old woman sustained a chest injury during a car crash. Upon admission, a physical examination revealed profuse swelling, inflammation, and deformation of the chest wall. An X-ray revealed an uncommon fracture of the manubrium at the manubriosternal joint. Which of the following is the most likely to be involved in such an injury? (repeated)

questions.question: A 37-year-old house painter fell from a ladder and fractured his left 4th rib and the structures which articulates with it. Which of the following structures would most likely be damaged?
questions.explanation: A (body of T3) — Rib 4 head articulates with T3 and T4 bodies (and disc); T5 (B) and a transverse process (C) are not its head joint. Key issue: the stem says “structures which articulates with it”; answer is incomplete because T4 body/disc also articulate.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 37-year-old house painter fell from a ladder and fractured his left 4th rib and the structures which articulates with it. Which of the following structures would most likely be damaged? (repeated)

questions.question: What syndrome is associated with the cervical rib?
questions.explanation: B (thoracic outlet syndrome) — A cervical rib narrows the thoracic outlet; carpal tunnel, Horner syndrome, and Guillain–Barré are not its defining syndrome.
questions.sourceQuestion: What syndrome is associated with the cervical rib? (repeated)

questions.question: Which of the following ribs are attached directly to the sternum via their costal cartilages?
questions.explanation: A (true ribs) — Ribs 1–7 attach directly to sternum; false ribs (B) attach indirectly or not at all, floating ribs (C) have no sternal attachment.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following ribs are attached directly to the sternum via their costal cartilages?

questions.question: A person sustains an injury and fractures his 4th rib, what structure is most likely going to be damaged?
questions.explanation: D (body of T3) — Rib 4 head articulates with T3 and T4 bodies; the tubercle articulates with T4 transverse process. Key issue: printed D is only one of the two head articulations; options omit T4 body and phrase the stem ambiguously.
questions.sourceQuestion: A person sustains an injury and fractures his 4th rib, what structure is most likely going to be damaged?

questions.question: Dislocation of the 4th vertebrae will cause an injury in which region?
questions.explanation: Ambiguous — B is the printed key. The head of rib 5 articulates with the inferior demifacet of T4. A also articulates with the body of T4 via its superior demifacet, and C articulates with the T4 transverse process. D is neither of those joint surfaces. The stem needs to specify which T4 articulation or injury pattern.
questions.sourceQuestion: Dislocation of the 4th vertebrae will cause an injury in which region? (repeated)

questions.question: A 2nd year medical student was doing her physical examination. She was asked to locate the 4th intercostal space. Which one of the following landmarks is the reference point to determine the intercostal spaces?
questions.explanation: A (manubriosternal joint) — Sternal angle locates rib 2, then spaces are counted down; sternocostal, vertebral, and costoclavicular joints are not the standard landmark.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 2nd year medical student was doing her physical examination. She was asked to locate the 4th intercostal space. Which one of the following landmarks is the reference point to determine the intercostal spaces?

questions.question: The tubercle of the 7th rib articulates with which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: E (transverse process of T7) — Rib 7 tubercle articulates with T7 transverse process; A–C are vertebral bodies and D is the wrong transverse level.
questions.sourceQuestion: The tubercle of the 7th rib articulates with which of the following structures? (repeated)

questions.question: At which rib level is the sternal angle located?
questions.explanation: B (2nd rib) — Costal cartilage 2 meets the sternal angle; levels 1, 3, 4, and 5 are inferior/superior to it.
questions.sourceQuestion: At which rib level is the sternal angle located? (repeated)

questions.question: A student palpates from the jugular notch down to the sternal angle. This corresponds to which of the following ribs?
questions.explanation: A (2nd rib) — The sternal angle is where the second rib is palpated; ribs 3–5 do not meet the angle.
questions.sourceQuestion: A student palpates from the jugular notch down to the sternal angle. This corresponds to which of the following ribs? (repeated)

questions.question: Which of the following vessels is compressed by the cervical rib?
questions.explanation: A (subclavian artery) — Cervical ribs may compress subclavian artery and lower plexus; carotid, external jugular, and superior thyroid vessels are not the typical compression.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following vessels is compressed by the cervical rib?

questions.question: Which of the following is seen in the sternal angle?
options: Opening of the inferior vena cava
Origin of the common carotid artery
questions.explanation: A (tracheal bifurcation) — The carina is near the transverse thoracic plane at the sternal angle; the other listed great-vessel/IVC landmarks are not there.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following is seen in the sternal angle?

questions.question: Which of the following structures articulate with the head of the sixth rib?
options: The inferior demifacet of T5 and superior demifacet of T6
The inferior facet of T5 and superior facet of T6
The inferior demifacet of T5 and superior facet of T6
questions.explanation: A (inferior demifacet T5 + superior demifacet T6) — Rib 6 head articulates with adjacent vertebral bodies/disk; whole facets (B,C) misname the costal demifacets and C omits the T6 demifacet.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following structures articulate with the head of the sixth rib?

questions.question: A 45-year-old man suffering from thoracic outlet syndrome (TOS). In clinical context, which of the following is the correct definition of the thoracic outlet?
options: The gap between the crura of the diaphragm
The gap between the sternal and costal origins of the diaphragm
The lower opening in the thoracic cage
The esophageal opening in the diaphragm
The upper opening in the thoracic cage
questions.explanation: E (upper thoracic aperture) — Anatomical thoracic outlet refers to the superior thoracic aperture; diaphragm gaps/openings (A,B,D) and the inferior opening (C) are different structures. Key issue: clinical “thoracic outlet” is commonly used for the cervicoaxillary passage, so wording is imprecise.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 45-year-old man suffering from thoracic outlet syndrome (TOS). In clinical context, which of the following is the correct definition of the thoracic outlet?

questions.question: A 31-year-old man came in with a tingling sensation. X-ray shows the presence of a cervical rib. Which of the following structures is most likely compressed?
questions.explanation: C (T1 spinal nerve) — Same cervical-rib/lower plexus compression as Q1; brachiocephalic vein, carotids, and vagus are not typical.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 31-year-old man came in with a tingling sensation. X-ray shows the presence of a cervical rib. Which of the following structures is most likely compressed?

questions.question: A boy suffered a fracture of the 4th rib and damage to its articulating surfaces. What structure is most likely affected?
options: The transverse processes of the 3rd thoracic vertebrae
The body of the 3rd thoracic vertebrae
The spinous process of the 4th thoracic vertebrae
The body of the 5th thoracic vertebrae
questions.explanation: B (body of T3) — Rib 4 head articulates with T3/T4 bodies; transverse process T3 articulates with rib 3, spinous T4 does not articulate with a rib, and T5 is not the relevant level. Key issue: T4 body is also a correct articulation but absent.
questions.sourceQuestion: A boy suffered a fracture of the 4th rib and damage to its articulating surfaces. What structure is most likely affected?

questions.question: A 32-year-old woman sustained a chest injury during a car crash. Upon admission of the patient to the hospital, a physical examination revealed profuse swelling, inflammation, and deformation of the chest wall. An X-ray revealed an uncommon fracture of the sternum at the manubriosternal joint. Which of the following ribs is most likely to be involved in such an injury?
questions.explanation: C (second rib) — Same sternal-angle landmark as Q2/Q10; first, third, fourth, and fifth ribs do not meet that junction.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 32-year-old woman sustained a chest injury during a car crash. Upon admission of the patient to the hospital, a physical examination revealed profuse swelling, inflammation, and deformation of the chest wall. An X-ray revealed an uncommon fracture of the sternum at the manubriosternal joint. Which of the following ribs is most likely to be involved in such an injury?

questions.question: A 32-year-old woman with a history of neck pain and numbness in her hand undergoes imaging. A cervical rib is discovered. This anomaly is associated with which vertebra?
questions.explanation: A (C7) — A cervical rib usually arises from C7; C5/C6 and T1/T2 are not the usual origin.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 32-year-old woman with a history of neck pain and numbness in her hand undergoes imaging. A cervical rib is discovered. This anomaly is associated with which vertebra?

questions.question: A penetrating injury occurs at the 5th left intercostal space at the midclavicular line. Which cardiac chamber is most likely to be directly injured?
questions.explanation: B (left ventricle) — The LV forms the apex and is palpable at left 5th ICS MCL; atria and RV are not directly beneath this point.
questions.sourceQuestion: A penetrating injury occurs at the 5th left intercostal space at the midclavicular line. Which cardiac chamber is most likely to be directly injured?

questions.question: During a cardiac surgery, a surgeon passes clamp posterior to the ascending aorta and the pulmonary trunk, but anterior to the superior vena cava. Through which space is the clamp being passed?
questions.explanation: D (transverse pericardial sinus) — It passes behind ascending aorta/pulmonary trunk and in front of SVC; oblique sinus is posterior to LA, while grooves and anterior mediastinum are not this passage.
questions.sourceQuestion: During a cardiac surgery, a surgeon passes clamp posterior to the ascending aorta and the pulmonary trunk, but anterior to the superior vena cava. Through which space is the clamp being passed?

questions.question: Which of the following structures will form the sternocostal surface of the heart?
questions.explanation: B (right ventricle) — RV makes most of the sternocostal/anterior surface; atria and LV contribute less or other surfaces.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following structures will form the sternocostal surface of the heart? (repeated)

questions.question: A patient has a replacement of Aorta, and it is connected to the heart-lung machine. What structure would you not be able to feel if you went into the oblique sinus?
questions.explanation: A (pulmonary trunk) — The oblique sinus is a blind recess behind the LA between pulmonary veins/IVC; pulmonary trunk is anterior and outside it. Other choices border or lie posteriorly to the recess. Printed key A is correct.
questions.sourceQuestion: A patient has a replacement of Aorta, and it is connected to the heart-lung machine. What structure would you not be able to feel if you went into the oblique sinus?

questions.question: The base of the heart is separated from the diaphragmatic surface by which of the following?
options: Posterior part of the coronary sulcus
Anterior part of the coronary sulcus
questions.explanation: A (posterior coronary sulcus) — The coronary sulcus separates atria from ventricles and its posterior segment divides base from diaphragmatic surface; other sulci separate ventricular chambers/surfaces.
questions.sourceQuestion: The base of the heart is separated from the diaphragmatic surface by which of the following?

questions.question: A patient complained of chest pain and had abnormal pulsations at midclavicular 5th intercostal space. Which part of the heart is most likely responsible for this pulsation?
questions.explanation: D (apex) — The LV apex produces the apical impulse at 5th ICS MCL; valves and RV are not the point of maximal impulse.
questions.sourceQuestion: A patient complained of chest pain and had abnormal pulsations at midclavicular 5th intercostal space. Which part of the heart is most likely responsible for this pulsation? (repeated)

questions.question: A patient with Cardiac Tamponade enters the ER. The Doctor needs to drain the pericardial Cavity. He uses the subxiphoid approach, but goes too deep and penetrates the visceral pericardium of which of the following heart chambers?
questions.explanation: B (right ventricle) — The subxiphoid pericardiocentesis route approaches the pericardial sac over the RV; LV, atria are not immediately behind the typical entry.
questions.sourceQuestion: A patient with Cardiac Tamponade enters the ER. The Doctor needs to drain the pericardial Cavity. He uses the subxiphoid approach, but goes too deep and penetrates the visceral pericardium of which of the following heart chambers?

questions.question: A surgeon was exploring the transverse sinus and wanted to clamp the aorta . He will put his hand in front of which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: A (SVC) — The transverse sinus lies posterior to arterial outflow vessels and anterior to SVC; IVC/pulmonary veins are not the vessel immediately behind the finger.
questions.sourceQuestion: A surgeon was exploring the transverse sinus and wanted to clamp the aorta . He will put his hand in front of which of the following structures?

questions.question: A surgeon put his index finger in the opening of the transverse sinus , his index finger attached to 2 great vessels ?
questions.explanation: C (aorta and pulmonary trunk) — These two arterial trunks bound the anterior side of the transverse sinus; SVC/IVC choices are not the paired anterior vessels.
questions.sourceQuestion: A surgeon put his index finger in the opening of the transverse sinus , his index finger attached to 2 great vessels ?

questions.question: A 34-year-old patient presents to the emergency department complaining of sharp chest pain that radiates to their left shoulder. A pericardial friction rub is heard upon auscultation, and the patient is diagnosed with acute pericarditis. Which nerve fibers carry the somatic pain sensation responsible for this specific radiation?
questions.explanation: B (phrenic nerve) — Fibers from C3–C5 carry somatic pain from fibrous/parietal pericardium and refer it to shoulder; vagus/pharyngeal nerves are visceral/autonomic, intercostals do not account for classic shoulder referral.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 34-year-old patient presents to the emergency department complaining of sharp chest pain that radiates to their left shoulder. A pericardial friction rub is heard upon auscultation, and the patient is diagnosed with acute pericarditis. Which nerve fibers carry the somatic pain sensation responsible for this specific radiation?

questions.question: A 42 year old woman is admitted to the emergency department after a fall from the balcony of her apartment. During physical examination there is an absence of heart sounds, reduced systolic pressure, reduced cardiac output, and engorged jugular veins. Which condition is most likely characterized by these signs?
questions.explanation: B (cardiac tamponade) — Effusion compresses heart, causing hypotension, low output, and JVD; the other thoracic/vascular conditions do not create this triad.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 42 year old woman is admitted to the emergency department after a fall from the balcony of her apartment. During physical examination there is an absence of heart sounds, reduced systolic pressure, reduced cardiac output, and engorged jugular veins. Which condition is most likely characterized by these signs?

questions.question: The apex beat of the heart can best be observed at which of the following spaces?
options: Left side adjacent to the sternum in the second intercostal space
Left side adjacent to the sternum in the fifth intercostal space
Left side in the midclavicular line in the fifth intercostal space
Right side adjacent to the sternum in the second intercostal space
Right side adjacent to the sternum in the fourth intercostal space
questions.explanation: C (left 5th ICS MCL) — This is the normal apex beat; other sites are not the apical impulse.
questions.sourceQuestion: The apex beat of the heart can best be observed at which of the following spaces? (repeated)

questions.question: In the anatomical position which of the following forms the base of the heart?
questions.explanation: B (left atrium) — LA forms most of the posterior base; right atrium, ventricles, and LV form other borders/surfaces.
questions.sourceQuestion: In the anatomical position which of the following forms the base of the heart?

questions.question: What is the blind end at the base of the heart?
questions.explanation: B (oblique sinus) — It is the blind pericardial recess behind the LA; transverse sinus is a passage, grooves and coronary sinus are not blind recesses.
questions.sourceQuestion: What is the blind end at the base of the heart?

questions.question: During a heart transplant procedure, the surgeon inserted his left index finger through the transverse pericardial sinus and then pulled forward on the two large vessels lying ventral to his fingers. Which vessels were these?
options: Pulmonary trunk and superior vena cava
Superior vena cava and right pulmonary artery
questions.explanation: B (pulmonary trunk and aorta) — They lie anterior to a finger in the transverse sinus; the other pairs do not both bound its anterior side.
questions.sourceQuestion: During a heart transplant procedure, the surgeon inserted his left index finger through the transverse pericardial sinus and then pulled forward on the two large vessels lying ventral to his fingers. Which vessels were these?

questions.question: The oblique pericardial sinus is located between which one the following?
options: Pulmonary veins and inferior vena cava
Pulmonary veins and superior vena cava
questions.explanation: B (pulmonary veins and IVC) — Oblique sinus lies behind LA, bounded by reflections around pulmonary veins and IVC; arterial trunks and SVC are not its boundaries.
questions.sourceQuestion: The oblique pericardial sinus is located between which one the following?

questions.question: The posterior interventricular artery runs on which surface?
questions.explanation: B (diaphragmatic surface) — The posterior interventricular artery runs in the posterior IV sulcus on the diaphragmatic surface; “posterior” can describe the sulcus, but among choices B is the surface. Key issue: A and B overlap anatomically; wording makes this ambiguous.
questions.sourceQuestion: The posterior interventricular artery runs on which surface?

questions.question: The coronary sulcus separates what structures?
options: Right atriums and ventricles from Left atriums and ventricles
questions.explanation: D (atria from ventricles) — Coronary sulcus is the AV groove; it does not separate right from left atria/ventricles.
questions.sourceQuestion: The coronary sulcus separates what structures? (repeated)

questions.question: Where is the posterior interventricular sulcus located?
questions.explanation: A (inferior surface) — Posterior IV sulcus lies mainly on the diaphragmatic/inferior surface; it is not the sternocostal surface, apex, or base.
questions.sourceQuestion: Where is the posterior interventricular sulcus located?

questions.question: Which of the following nerves would be affected if the pericardium is irritated?
questions.explanation: A (phrenic nerve) — Pericardial irritation can affect phrenic nerve; other listed nerves do not supply fibrous/parietal pericardium.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following nerves would be affected if the pericardium is irritated?

questions.question: What structure is directly posterior to the retrosternal space in a lateral chest X-ray?
questions.explanation: C (right ventricle) — RV is directly behind the sternum/retrosternal space; trachea and great veins are higher/posterior.
questions.sourceQuestion: What structure is directly posterior to the retrosternal space in a lateral chest X-ray?

questions.question: What structure lies immediately posterior to the left atrium?
questions.explanation: A (esophagus) — LA is immediately anterior to esophagus; LV, pulmonary trunk, IVC and left main bronchus are not the closest posterior relation.
questions.sourceQuestion: What structure lies immediately posterior to the left atrium?

questions.question: Which of the labeled structures in the given PA radiograph of the chest indicates the aortic arch?
questions.explanation: D — Aortic arch. On the frontal chest radiograph, D is the upper contour on the patient’s left (viewer’s right). A sits by the tracheal air column, B is the right cardiac border, C is the right cardiophrenic angle, and E is at the left ventricular contour. The printed key is supported.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the labeled structures in the given PA radiograph of the chest indicates the aortic arch?

questions.question: During a heart transplant procedure, the surgeon inserted his left index finger through the transverse pericardial sinus. Which one of the following vessels lies dorsal to the index finger?
questions.explanation: D (SVC) — SVC is dorsal/posterior to the transverse sinus; aorta and pulmonary trunk are ventral, other veins are not adjacent.
questions.sourceQuestion: During a heart transplant procedure, the surgeon inserted his left index finger through the transverse pericardial sinus. Which one of the following vessels lies dorsal to the index finger?

questions.question: A water-bottle-shaped cardiac silhouette on a conventional chest X-ray is classically seen in which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: C (pericardial effusion) — Large effusion can produce a globular “water-bottle” silhouette; pneumothorax, heart failure, PE, and isolated LVH do not classically do so.
questions.sourceQuestion: A water-bottle-shaped cardiac silhouette on a conventional chest X-ray is classically seen in which of the following conditions?

questions.question: Which of the following veins accompanies the left anterior descending (LAD)?
questions.explanation: A (great cardiac vein) — It accompanies LAD in anterior interventricular groove; middle cardiac vein accompanies posterior IV artery, small cardiac vein follows right marginal region, SVC/coronary sinus are not the companion along LAD.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following veins accompanies the left anterior descending (LAD)?

questions.question: During Cardiac Surgery, a surgeon inserts a finger into the transverse pericardial sinus. Which Structure lies anterior to the surgeon's finger?
questions.explanation: E (pulmonary trunk) — Pulmonary trunk is anterior to a finger in transverse sinus; LA and caval/aortic posterior structures lie behind or outside.
questions.sourceQuestion: During Cardiac Surgery, a surgeon inserts a finger into the transverse pericardial sinus. Which Structure lies anterior to the surgeon's finger?

questions.question: A 41-year-old man is admitted to the emergency department with complaints of shortness of breath, dizziness, and sharp chest pain. The large arrow in his chest radiograph indicates the region of pathology. What is this structure? (Please see the attached picture)
questions.explanation: E — Aortic knuckle. The arrow points to the upper left mediastinal prominence. A is lower at the pulmonary artery segment, B borders the right diaphragm, C is near the upper right mediastinum, and D shapes the lower left cardiac silhouette.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 41-year-old man is admitted to the emergency department with complaints of shortness of breath, dizziness, and sharp chest pain. The large arrow in his chest radiograph indicates the region of pathology. What is this structure? (Please see the attached picture)

questions.question: A patient has a tricuspid murmur. Best place to hear it?
questions.explanation: A (lower sternal border) — Tricuspid sound is best at left lower sternal border; apex is mitral, right 2nd ICS aortic, left 2nd ICS pulmonary.
questions.sourceQuestion: A patient has a tricuspid murmur. Best place to hear it? (repeated)

questions.question: A 50-year-old man who has been overweight and sedentary most of his life experiences shortness of breath and cyanosis on exertion when he attempts to start an exercise program for the first time. A thorough physical examination by his physician reveals an aortic valve defect and an aortic murmur. This murmur is best detected when the stethoscope is placed over which of the indicated sites?
questions.explanation: B (right 2nd ICS) — Aortic valve is auscultated at right 2nd intercostal space; other sites are pulmonary, tricuspid, or mitral areas.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 50-year-old man who has been overweight and sedentary most of his life experiences shortness of breath and cyanosis on exertion when he attempts to start an exercise program for the first time. A thorough physical examination by his physician reveals an aortic valve defect and an aortic murmur. This murmur is best detected when the stethoscope is placed over which of the indicated sites? (repeated)

questions.question: A 58-year-old man presents with dyspnea. Examination reveals a mitral valve stenosis / mitral regurgitation murmur. At which of the following locations is auscultation of this valve best performed?
options: Above the medial third of the left clavicle
At the left fifth intercostal space, midclavicular line
At the left second intercostal space, just lateral to the sternum
At the right second intercostal space, just lateral to the sternum
questions.explanation: C (left 5th ICS MCL) — Mitral sounds transmit best at the apex; clavicle/sternal angle and second spaces are not the mitral listening point.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 58-year-old man presents with dyspnea. Examination reveals a mitral valve stenosis / mitral regurgitation murmur. At which of the following locations is auscultation of this valve best performed? (repeated)

questions.question: The septomarginal trabeculae (Moderator band) plays a role in the conductance of which of the following?
questions.explanation: C (right bundle branch) — Moderator band carries the right bundle branch to anterior papillary muscle; left bundle/AV/SA nodes are not transmitted through it.
questions.sourceQuestion: The septomarginal trabeculae (Moderator band) plays a role in the conductance of which of the following?

questions.question: Which of the following is the auscultation point for the pulmonary valve?
options: 2nd intercostal space at right sternal border
2nd intercostal space at the left sternal border
3rd intercostal space at right sternal border
5th intercostal space at lower sternal border
questions.explanation: B (left 2nd ICS sternal border) — Pulmonary valve auscultation point; right 2nd ICS is aortic, lower sternal border tricuspid, apex mitral.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following is the auscultation point for the pulmonary valve?

questions.question: What structure in the right atrium marks the boundary between the rough pectinate muscle and the smooth wall?
questions.explanation: D (crista terminalis) — It divides smooth sinus venarum from pectinate-muscle atrial wall; septum/fossa ovalis, chordae, and Eustachian valve do not form that boundary.
questions.sourceQuestion: What structure in the right atrium marks the boundary between the rough pectinate muscle and the smooth wall?

questions.question: A 3-year-old girl undergoes corrective surgery to repair a small ventricular septal defect (VSD). To gain access to the site, an incision is made in the anterior surface of the right atrium so instruments may be inserted through the tricuspid valve to repair the VSD. Which of the following structures is the most important to protect as the incision is made in the right atrium?
questions.explanation: B (crista terminalis) — It is in the RA and could be injured during an anterior RA incision; moderator band/trabeculae/papillary muscle are in RV, infundibulum is RV outflow.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 3-year-old girl undergoes corrective surgery to repair a small ventricular septal defect (VSD). To gain access to the site, an incision is made in the anterior surface of the right atrium so instruments may be inserted through the tricuspid valve to repair the VSD. Which of the following structures is the most important to protect as the incision is made in the right atrium?

questions.question: Where can we auscultate the Mitral Valve?
questions.explanation: D (left 5th ICS MCL) — Mitral auscultation at apex; right/left 2nd spaces and left sternal border are not the site.
questions.sourceQuestion: Where can we auscultate the Mitral Valve? (repeated)

questions.question: Where can we auscultate the Aortic Valve?
options: At the Apex of the heart
questions.explanation: D (right 2nd ICS) — Aortic listening area; apex and left 2nd ICS are mitral/pulmonary, 4th–5th is not standard aortic.
questions.sourceQuestion: Where can we auscultate the Aortic Valve? (repeated)

questions.question: Which of the following can you find inside an adult heart?
questions.explanation: B (fossa ovalis) — Adult interatrial septum bears the fossa ovalis, remnant of fetal foramen ovale; fetal septa/horns are not normal adult openings.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following can you find inside an adult heart?

questions.question: Which valve is auscultated at the 2nd intercostal spaces at the left sternal border?
questions.explanation: D (pulmonary valve) — Left 2nd ICS sternal border is pulmonary; the other valves have different auscultation points.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which valve is auscultated at the 2nd intercostal spaces at the left sternal border? (repeated)

questions.question: Which valve has 3 cusps (anterior, left, right)?
questions.explanation: A (pulmonary) — Pulmonary valve has anterior, right, and left cusps; aortic has right/left/posterior, tricuspid three named cusps, mitral two.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which valve has 3 cusps (anterior, left, right)?

questions.question: Which special structure is found in the right atrium?
questions.explanation: A (pectinate muscle) — Pectinate muscles are in atria (especially RA auricle); trabeculae carneae and papillary muscles are ventricular, coronary sinus is an opening rather than a special wall feature. Key issue: coronary sinus is also located/opening in RA, so question is not uniquely worded; A is intended.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which special structure is found in the right atrium? (repeated)

questions.question: Where is the crista terminalis found?
questions.explanation: A (right atrium) — Crista terminalis is a RA ridge; it is absent from ventricles and LA.
questions.sourceQuestion: Where is the crista terminalis found?

questions.question: At the apex of the heart, the mitral valve is present, where is that exactly?
options: 5th intercostal space lateral to the sternum
5th intercostal space at the midclavicular line
questions.explanation: B (left 5th ICS MCL) — Mitral listening/apex point; 5th ICS beside sternum and second-space/right-sided locations are wrong.
questions.sourceQuestion: At the apex of the heart, the mitral valve is present, where is that exactly?

questions.question: Which of the following structures is present in the right ventricle?
questions.explanation: B (moderator band) — It is a right ventricular trabecula carrying right bundle branch; crista/fossa/coronary sinus/pulmonary veins belong to atria.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following structures is present in the right ventricle?

questions.question: The cusps of the atrioventricular valves are anchored to the papillary muscles by which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: C (chordae tendineae) — Chordae connect AV valve cusps to papillary muscles; epicardium, fossa, endocardium and pericardium do not tether cusps.
questions.sourceQuestion: The cusps of the atrioventricular valves are anchored to the papillary muscles by which of the following structures?

questions.question: A final-year medical student was doing a physical examination of the cardiovascular system. In order to properly place her stethoscope to listen to a murmur from aortic valve she needs to place the stethoscope in:
questions.explanation: A (right 2nd ICS) — Aortic listening point; left 2nd pulmonary, left 5th mitral, other sites not standard.
questions.sourceQuestion: A final-year medical student was doing a physical examination of the cardiovascular system. In order to properly place her stethoscope to listen to a murmur from aortic valve she needs to place the stethoscope in:

questions.question: Identify the cardiac chamber with the filling defect marked by the red arrow in the cardiac CT?
questions.explanation: B — Left atrium. The filling defect is in the thin-walled posterior chamber just anterior to the oesophagus. A is right-sided, C is anterior, and D has thicker muscle and lies more anterolaterally.
questions.sourceQuestion: Identify the cardiac chamber with the filling defect marked by the red arrow in the cardiac CT?

questions.question: A 62-year-old man came for an X-ray and was diagnosed with an aortic aneurysm.The patient gradually has a change in his voice. Which nerve did this affect?
questions.explanation: B (left recurrent laryngeal nerve) — It loops under aortic arch and can be compressed by aneurysm, causing hoarseness; vagus, right recurrent, sympathetic, phrenic are not the typical relation.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 62-year-old man came for an X-ray and was diagnosed with an aortic aneurysm.The patient gradually has a change in his voice. Which nerve did this affect? (Repeated 2X)

questions.question: The small cardiac vein runs parallel to which artery?
questions.explanation: E (right marginal artery) — Small cardiac vein commonly accompanies the right marginal artery; LAD is accompanied by great cardiac vein, posterior IV by middle cardiac vein, circumflex by great vein in AV groove.
questions.sourceQuestion: The small cardiac vein runs parallel to which artery?

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding right coronary dominance?
questions.explanation: C (posterior interventricular artery from RCA) — Right dominance means RCA gives posterior IV artery; LAD arises from LCA in either dominance, so A/D are false; B reverses origin.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following is true regarding right coronary dominance? (repeated)

questions.question: A patient developed myocardial infarction following occlusion of the circumflex branch of the left coronary artery. Which of the following areas of the heart is likely to be affected?
options: Apex of the heart and interventricular septum
questions.explanation: A (LA and LV) — Circumflex supplies much of lateral/posterior LV and LA; LAD mainly anterior septum/apex, RCA supplies right heart.
questions.sourceQuestion: A patient developed myocardial infarction following occlusion of the circumflex branch of the left coronary artery. Which of the following areas of the heart is likely to be affected? (Repeated)

questions.question: Which of the following represents the posterior descending interventricular artery?
questions.explanation: B — Diagram label D. D indicates the branch on the inferior/posterior aspect running toward the interventricular groove. Diagram B and C are by the proximal left branches, A is on the right AV groove, and E marks the long anterior interventricular course.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following represents the posterior descending interventricular artery?

questions.question: Which vessel supplies the Right and Left Bundle Branches?
questions.explanation: B (anterior interventricular/LAD) — Septal branches of LAD supply bundle branches; PIA, circumflex, and RCA are not the usual main supply to both bundles.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which vessel supplies the Right and Left Bundle Branches? (repeated)

questions.question: In a balanced coronary artery pattern, the blood supply to most of the interventricular Septum in most people is derived from which of the following?
questions.explanation: B (anterior interventricular artery) — LAD supplies anterior two-thirds of septum and thus most septal myocardium; PIA supplies posterior third, RCA/circumflex territory is more limited.
questions.sourceQuestion: In a balanced coronary artery pattern, the blood supply to most of the interventricular Septum in most people is derived from which of the following?

questions.question: As a cardiology resident, you’re concerned about the blockage of the artery to the SA node in a patient. This artery typically arises from which of the following?
questions.explanation: D (RCA) — SA nodal artery most often comes from RCA; marginal, PIA, and LAD are less typical origins.
questions.sourceQuestion: As a cardiology resident, you’re concerned about the blockage of the artery to the SA node in a patient. This artery typically arises from which of the following? (repeated)

questions.question: There was a block in the circumflex coronary artery; blood flow to which of the following decreases significantly?
questions.explanation: B (LA and LV) — Circumflex supplies left atrium and lateral LV; right atrium/ventricle and septum are primarily other coronary territories.
questions.sourceQuestion: There was a block in the circumflex coronary artery; blood flow to which of the following decreases significantly?

questions.question: In the most common right-dominant pattern of coronary artery, which one of the following statements applies?
options: Posterior interventricular artery is a branch of right coronary artery
Left coronary artery supplies more blood to the right ventricle
Posterior interventricular branch is a branch from the left coronary artery
Right coronary artery supplies the anterior part of interventricular septum
Left coronary artery supplies the SA node
questions.explanation: A (PIA is branch of RCA) — This defines right dominance; left coronary supplies left-sided territory and LAD supplies anterior septum, not posterior branch.
questions.sourceQuestion: In the most common right-dominant pattern of coronary artery, which one of the following statements applies?

questions.question: An elderly lady died from a coronary occlusion. The autopsy showed a damaged anterior portion of the interventricular septum. Which one of the following arteries is most likely involved?
questions.explanation: C (LAD) — LAD supplies anterior IV septum; marginal, circumflex, RCA, and PIA are not the primary anterior septal supply.
questions.sourceQuestion: An elderly lady died from a coronary occlusion. The autopsy showed a damaged anterior portion of the interventricular septum. Which one of the following arteries is most likely involved?

questions.question: Occlusion of which of the following might result in a complete heart block (that is, the right and left bundles of the conduction system have been damaged)?
questions.explanation: E (LAD) — Septal perforators supply both bundle branches; marginal/circumflex/RCA choices are less direct, and “right diagonal” is not a standard named coronary branch. Key issue: complete heart block can have multiple arterial causes; LAD is intended given bundle injury.
questions.sourceQuestion: Occlusion of which of the following might result in a complete heart block (that is, the right and left bundles of the conduction system have been damaged)?

questions.question: A guy presented to the ER with chest pain radiating to the shoulder. Angiography concluded complete blockage of left coronary artery if the person is left dominant, which of the following statements is correct?
options: Ischemia of anterior ⅔ of interventricular septum
Ischemia of the whole interventricular septum
Ischemia of posterior ⅓ of interventricular septum
questions.explanation: B (whole IV septum) — In left dominance, LCA supplies both anterior septum via LAD and posterior septum via circumflex-derived PIA; other choices are partial septum or RV.
questions.sourceQuestion: A guy presented to the ER with chest pain radiating to the shoulder. Angiography concluded complete blockage of left coronary artery if the person is left dominant, which of the following statements is correct?

questions.question: A 7-year-old boy with Down syndrome underwent surgery to repair a congenital ventricular septal defect. During this procedure, iatrogenic injury to the coronary artery supplying the conduction system of the heart, including the sinoatrial (SA) and atrioventricular (AV) nodes, occurred, resulting in heart block. What artery was most likely damaged by this surgeon?
questions.explanation: D (RCA) — SA and AV nodal arteries most commonly derive from RCA; circumflex can supply them variably, while LAD/marginal are not usual for both nodes. Key issue: not uniquely guaranteed because nodal artery origins vary, particularly SA node.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 7-year-old boy with Down syndrome underwent surgery to repair a congenital ventricular septal defect. During this procedure, iatrogenic injury to the coronary artery supplying the conduction system of the heart, including the sinoatrial (SA) and atrioventricular (AV) nodes, occurred, resulting in heart block. What artery was most likely damaged by this surgeon?

questions.question: A 58-year-old man presented in the ER with chest pain. His angiography revealed 90% stenosis of anterior interventricular (LAD) artery. Which portion of the heart is most likely susceptible to damage?
options: Posterior one third of the interventricular septum
Anterior two thirds of the interventricular septum
questions.explanation: B (anterior two-thirds septum) — LAD septal branches supply anterior septum; posterior third, diaphragmatic LV, RA, and AV node are not its main territory.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 58-year-old man presented in the ER with chest pain. His angiography revealed 90% stenosis of anterior interventricular (LAD) artery. Which portion of the heart is most likely susceptible to damage?

questions.question: What vein runs with the vessel shown in the diagram below?
questions.explanation: B (great cardiac vein) — It accompanies LAD in anterior IV groove; middle vein accompanies PIA, anterior veins drain RV, small vein follows right margin, coronary sinus is posterior collecting channel.
questions.sourceQuestion: What vein runs with the vessel shown in the diagram below?

questions.question: A person has a posterior interventricular ischemia. Which artery is occluded?
questions.explanation: E — Posterior interventricular artery is the intended vessel. It supplies the posterior septal territory. A–D are labelled elsewhere on the coronary tree. The small image shows predominantly the anterior surface, so the brief distal course indicated by E is hard to verify in isolation.
questions.sourceQuestion: A person has a posterior interventricular ischemia. Which artery is occluded?

questions.question: Which of the following vessels accompanies the Left anterior descending artery?
questions.explanation: A (great cardiac vein) — Same LAD companion relationship; middle vein follows PIA, small cardiac nerve is not a vein, anterior vein drains RV.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following vessels accompanies the Left anterior descending artery? (Repeated)

questions.question: What does “left coronary dominance” mean in relation to the left coronary Artery?
options: It gives rise to the anterior interventricular (IV) artery
It is derived from the left 6th aortic arch
It supplies the right border of the heart
It gives rise to the posterior interventricular artery
It supplies the margin of the heart
questions.explanation: D (gives rise to PIA) — Left dominance means circumflex gives posterior IV artery; LAD arises from LCA regardless of dominance, while origin/territory options B/C/E do not define dominance.
questions.sourceQuestion: What does “left coronary dominance” mean in relation to the left coronary Artery?

questions.question: A 55-year-old man was diagnosed with recurrent chest pain, the coronary artery angiogram reveals 90% stenosis of the left anterior descending artery (LAD), based Upon this finding, which portion of the heart is most likely susceptible to ischemic damage?
options: Posterior one third of interventricular septum
Anterior two thirds of interventricular septum
questions.explanation: E (anterior two-thirds septum) — LAD ischemia compromises anterior septum; RA, AV node, posterior third and inferior LV are not primary LAD territory.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 55-year-old man was diagnosed with recurrent chest pain, the coronary artery angiogram reveals 90% stenosis of the left anterior descending artery (LAD), based Upon this finding, which portion of the heart is most likely susceptible to ischemic damage? (repeated)

questions.question: There was a blockage of the posterior interventricular artery. What structure is primarily affected?
options: Membranous part of the interventricular septum
questions.explanation: A (membranous IV septum) — PIA supplies posterior septum including nearby membranous region; posterior interatrial septum and ventricular free walls are not its main target. Key issue: His bundle lies in membranous septum, but PIA occlusion is not a reliably exclusive supply to it.
questions.sourceQuestion: There was a blockage of the posterior interventricular artery. What structure is primarily affected?

questions.question: Which of the following veins is close to the posterior interventricular artery (PIA)?
questions.explanation: B (middle cardiac vein) — It accompanies PIA in posterior IV sulcus; great vein accompanies LAD, small vein follows right margin, SVC/coronary sinus do not accompany locally.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following veins is close to the posterior interventricular artery (PIA)? (repeated)

questions.question: A patient with a new holosystolic murmur suggests mitral regurgitation. Where should the stethoscope be placed to hear this murmur best?
options: Left half of the sternum at the fourth costal cartilage
Second right intercostal space at the sternal border
Lower left sternal border, fourth to fifth intercostal space
Fifth left intercostal space in the midclavicular line (apex)
Second left intercostal space at the sternal
questions.explanation: D (left 5th ICS MCL) — Mitral regurgitation best heard at apex; other locations correspond to other valves or are less specific.
questions.sourceQuestion: A patient with a new holosystolic murmur suggests mitral regurgitation. Where should the stethoscope be placed to hear this murmur best?

questions.question: A 62-year-old woman has a proximal LAD occlusion. Her ECG shows an anterior infarct and a new right bundle branch block. Which branches normally supply the affected conducting tissue?
options: Septal perforating branches of the LAD
questions.explanation: D (LAD septal perforators) — They supply right bundle and anterior septum; marginal, conus, AV nodal and diagonal branches are not the main septal conduction supply.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 62-year-old woman has a proximal LAD occlusion. Her ECG shows an anterior infarct and a new right bundle branch block. Which branches normally supply the affected conducting tissue?

questions.question: A 58-year-old man presents with an acute inferior myocardial infarction. His ECG shows a new complete third-degree AV heart block. Angiography shows a right-dominant coronary circulation. Occlusion of which artery best explains both findings?
questions.explanation: C (RCA) — In right-dominant circulation RCA supplies inferior wall and usually AV nodal artery; left marginal/circumflex/LAD/diagonal do not explain both inferior MI and AV block as well.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 58-year-old man presents with an acute inferior myocardial infarction. His ECG shows a new complete third-degree AV heart block. Angiography shows a right-dominant coronary circulation. Occlusion of which artery best explains both findings?

questions.question: A 31-year-old male is suffering from a penetrating wound to the 8th intercostal space along the paravertebral line. The artery which supplies the intercostal space is bleeding. Which of the following vessels is this artery a branch of?
questions.explanation: A (descending thoracic aorta) — Posterior intercostal artery for spaces 3–11 arises from thoracic aorta; pulmonary, carotid, internal thoracic, and subclavian are not direct source here.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 31-year-old male is suffering from a penetrating wound to the 8th intercostal space along the paravertebral line. The artery which supplies the intercostal space is bleeding. Which of the following vessels is this artery a branch of? (Repeated)

questions.question: A kid was brought to the ER with headache and nose bleeding for 1–2 weeks. He had high blood pressure in the brachial artery and cold lower extremities (wearing socks in summer). What is your diagnosis?
questions.explanation: A (coarctation of aorta) — Upper-body hypertension with weak/cold lower limbs is classic coarctation; other congenital conditions do not produce this pressure gradient.
questions.sourceQuestion: A kid was brought to the ER with headache and nose bleeding for 1–2 weeks. He had high blood pressure in the brachial artery and cold lower extremities (wearing socks in summer). What is your diagnosis? (Repeated)

questions.question: The Internal Thoracic Artery runs along which line?
questions.explanation: A (parasternal line) — Internal thoracic artery descends just lateral to sternum; midclavicular, midsternal, and paravertebral are not its course.
questions.sourceQuestion: The Internal Thoracic Artery runs along which line?

questions.question: If the internal thoracic artery gets ligated and blood flow stops for intercostal spaces 3–6, which artery will provide the blood flow instead?
questions.explanation: B (posterior intercostal artery) — Posterior intercostals provide collateral supply to spaces 3–6 if internal thoracic inflow is lost; musculophrenic and superior epigastric supply lower/anterior regions.
questions.sourceQuestion: If the internal thoracic artery gets ligated and blood flow stops for intercostal spaces 3–6, which artery will provide the blood flow instead?

questions.question: A 30-year-old man is diagnosed with a blockage of arterial flow in the proximal part of the thoracic aorta. Brachial arterial pressure is markedly increased, femoral pressure is decreased, and the femoral pulses are delayed. The patient shows no external signs of inflammation. Which of the following does the patient have?
questions.explanation: A (coarctation of aorta) — Same upper/lower pressure discrepancy and delayed femoral pulses; aortic/mitral stenosis and aneurysm do not fit.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 30-year-old man is diagnosed with a blockage of arterial flow in the proximal part of the thoracic aorta. Brachial arterial pressure is markedly increased, femoral pressure is decreased, and the femoral pulses are delayed. The patient shows no external signs of inflammation. Which of the following does the patient have?

questions.question: A CT scan of a patient with a superior vena cava obstruction shows dilated posterior intercostal veins on the right side. Into which vein do these posterior intercostal veins normally drain?
questions.explanation: D (azygos vein) — Right posterior intercostal veins generally drain to azygos; hemiazygos drains left lower spaces, IVC/internal thoracic/subclavian are not typical direct channels.
questions.sourceQuestion: A CT scan of a patient with a superior vena cava obstruction shows dilated posterior intercostal veins on the right side. Into which vein do these posterior intercostal veins normally drain?

questions.question: A man has complained of changing of his voice, which of the following nerves might have been damaged leading to this change?
questions.explanation: A (left recurrent laryngeal nerve) — Injury causes hoarseness and the nerve loops under aortic arch; phrenic, vagus trunk, and intercostals are not the characteristic voice motor pathway.
questions.sourceQuestion: A man has complained of changing of his voice, which of the following nerves might have been damaged leading to this change?

questions.question: A man developed a tumor in his posterior mediastinum. Which of the following is probably compressed?
questions.explanation: A (vagus nerve) — Vagus traverses posterior mediastinum; arch of aorta/trachea are superior, azygos arch right-sided, phrenic anterior.
questions.sourceQuestion: A man developed a tumor in his posterior mediastinum. Which of the following is probably compressed?

questions.question: A medical student is learning about the right recurrent laryngeal nerve. The doctor mentions that the nerve loops around a certain vessel. Which vessel is the doctor referring to?
questions.explanation: A (right subclavian artery) — Right recurrent laryngeal loops under right subclavian; left nerve loops by aortic arch/ligamentum arteriosum, other choices not its turn.
questions.sourceQuestion: A medical student is learning about the right recurrent laryngeal nerve. The doctor mentions that the nerve loops around a certain vessel. Which vessel is the doctor referring to?

questions.question: A 73-year-old male developed a tumor in the posterior mediastinum. Which of the following structures is most likely to be compressed?
questions.explanation: D (thoracic duct) — It ascends in posterior mediastinum; arch of azygos/aorta, phrenic, trachea are not the most characteristic posterior structure. Key issue: posterior mediastinal tumors may compress several structures; stem lacks localization details.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 73-year-old male developed a tumor in the posterior mediastinum. Which of the following structures is most likely to be compressed?

questions.question: A 6-day-old newborn diagnosed with patent ductus arteriosus undergoes surgery to ligate it. Which of the following nerves is the surgeon protecting?
questions.explanation: B (left recurrent laryngeal nerve) — It passes by ductus arteriosus/ligamentum arteriosum and is at risk during PDA ligation; vagus/phrenic/right recurrent are not adjacent.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 6-day-old newborn diagnosed with patent ductus arteriosus undergoes surgery to ligate it. Which of the following nerves is the surgeon protecting?

questions.question: The usual approach is a longitudinal cut in the sternum. Which structure will be most at risk?
questions.explanation: B (internal thoracic artery) — It runs close to sternum and is vulnerable during median sternotomy; vagus/phrenic are lateral, intercostal arteries are not the midline structure.
questions.sourceQuestion: The usual approach is a longitudinal cut in the sternum. Which structure will be most at risk?

questions.question: A patient with an injury to the mandibular part of the sternum would most likely injure which of the following vessels?
questions.explanation: C (left brachiocephalic vein) — It crosses behind upper manubrium; subclavians and SVC are more lateral/caudal, right brachiocephalic is shorter and right-sided.
questions.sourceQuestion: A patient with an injury to the mandibular part of the sternum would most likely injure which of the following vessels?

questions.question: A medical student was trying to find the right recurrent laryngeal nerve. Where can he find this nerve?
questions.explanation: E (under right subclavian artery) — Right recurrent loops beneath it; ligamentum arteriosum is left-sided, pulmonary artery/pericardium/vein are not its loop.
questions.sourceQuestion: A medical student was trying to find the right recurrent laryngeal nerve. Where can he find this nerve? (Repeated)

questions.question: During an exploratory surgery, the surgeon elevates the esophagus off the vertebral bodies between the azygos vein and descending aorta. What structure was she most looking for?
questions.explanation: E (thoracic duct) — Duct ascends between azygos and aorta, posterior to esophagus; splanchnic nerve and sympathetic trunk are lateral, other choices do not occupy that midline interval.
questions.sourceQuestion: During an exploratory surgery, the surgeon elevates the esophagus off the vertebral bodies between the azygos vein and descending aorta. What structure was she most looking for?

questions.question: A tumor of the posterior mediastinum is most likely to compress which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: B (esophagus) — Posterior mediastinum contains esophagus; aortic arch, IVC and pulmonary trunk are not posterior mediastinal structures, trachea is superior mediastinum.
questions.sourceQuestion: A tumor of the posterior mediastinum is most likely to compress which of the following structures?

questions.question: An 8-year-old boy has a mid-line tumor on thymus impinging posteriorly on a blood vessel. What is the affected vessel?
questions.explanation: B (left brachiocephalic vein) — It lies behind manubrium/thymus and can be compressed by an enlarged thymus; other listed right vessels/jugulars are not directly posterior.
questions.sourceQuestion: An 8-year-old boy has a mid-line tumor on thymus impinging posteriorly on a blood vessel. What is the affected vessel?

questions.question: A 3-month-old infant after a car accident undergoes tracheostomy. Which structure is most at high risk of injury?
questions.explanation: A (left brachiocephalic vein) — It may cross anterior to trachea in infants and is vulnerable during tracheostomy; vagus, thoracic duct, carotid, phrenic are less directly anterior.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 3-month-old infant after a car accident undergoes tracheostomy. Which structure is most at high risk of injury?

questions.question: An 80-year-old man has a posterior mediastinal tumor. Which structure is compromised?
questions.explanation: C (thoracic duct) — It is a posterior mediastinal structure; aortic/azygos arches and phrenic nerve are not the best answer. Key issue: same broad ambiguity as Q4.
questions.sourceQuestion: An 80-year-old man has a posterior mediastinal tumor. Which structure is compromised?

questions.question: A large venous structure crossing midline obliquely from left into SVC is most likely which vessel?
questions.explanation: A (left brachiocephalic vein) — It crosses obliquely from left to right to join SVC; right brachiocephalic is short, other veins do not cross to SVC this way.
questions.sourceQuestion: A large venous structure crossing midline obliquely from left into SVC is most likely which vessel?

questions.question: A pediatric heart surgeon divides the sternum and sees a lobulated gland-like structure immediately obscuring the heart. What is this?
questions.explanation: A (thymus) — Thymus lies anteriorly behind sternum over heart/great vessels; lungs, thyroid, lymph nodes, liver are not this gland-like midline organ.
questions.sourceQuestion: A pediatric heart surgeon divides the sternum and sees a lobulated gland-like structure immediately obscuring the heart. What is this?

questions.question: A tumor causing edema in the arms with engorged neck veins and visible intercostal veins is suspected in which mediastinal region?
questions.explanation: D (superior mediastinum) — SVC/large veins occupy superior mediastinum; obstruction causes upper-body edema, JVD and collateral intercostal veins. Anterior/posterior mediastinum and diaphragmatic opening do not fit.
questions.sourceQuestion: A tumor causing edema in the arms with engorged neck veins and visible intercostal veins is suspected in which mediastinal region?

questions.question: Which of the following is seen at the sternal angle?
questions.explanation: A (tracheal bifurcation) — Carina lies near sternal angle; apex, diaphragm tendon, and great-vessel termination are not the key landmark.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following is seen at the sternal angle?

questions.question: A 62-year-old man came for an X-ray and was diagnosed with an aortic aneurysm. The patient gradually has a change in his voice. Which nerve did this affect?
questions.explanation: B (left recurrent laryngeal nerve) — Aortic arch aneurysm can compress nerve where it loops beneath arch; other listed nerves do not have that relation.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 62-year-old man came for an X-ray and was diagnosed with an aortic aneurysm. The patient gradually has a change in his voice. Which nerve did this affect?

questions.question: A 31-year-old male is suffering a penetrating wound through the 8th intercostal space along the paravertebral line. The artery that supplies the intercostal space is bleeding. This artery is a branch of which of the following vessels?
questions.explanation: D (descending thoracic aorta) — Posterior intercostal artery at 8th space arises from descending aorta; internal thoracic/subclavian supply anterior upper spaces, pulmonary/carotid are unrelated.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 31-year-old male is suffering a penetrating wound through the 8th intercostal space along the paravertebral line. The artery that supplies the intercostal space is bleeding. This artery is a branch of which of the following vessels?

questions.question: A patient has problems in his nasal cavity leading to the block of the superior meatus paranasal opening. Which paranasal cavity is affected?
questions.explanation: B (posterior ethmoidal cells) — They drain to superior meatus; anterior ethmoid/frontal/maxillary drain to middle meatus, nasociliary is not a sinus.
questions.sourceQuestion: A patient has problems in his nasal cavity leading to the block of the superior meatus paranasal opening. Which paranasal cavity is affected? (Repeated)

questions.question: Which of the following sinuses open onto superior Meatus
questions.explanation: D (posterior ethmoidal cells) — Same drainage; frontal, anterior/middle ethmoid, and maxillary open to middle meatus.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following sinuses open onto superior Meatus

questions.question: A 38-year-old man has had a thyroid surgery to remove his papillary carcinoma. The external laryngeal nerve that accompanies the superior thyroid artery is damaged during the surgery. This injury could result in a severe impairment of one of the following functions.
questions.explanation: C (tensing vocal cords) — External branch of superior laryngeal nerve supplies cricothyroid; other actions are mainly intrinsic laryngeal muscles supplied by recurrent laryngeal nerve.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 38-year-old man has had a thyroid surgery to remove his papillary carcinoma. The external laryngeal nerve that accompanies the superior thyroid artery is damaged during the surgery. This injury could result in a severe impairment of one of the following functions. (Repeated)

questions.question: A 53-year-old man has difficulty with breathing through his nose. On examination, his physician finds that he has swelling of the mucous membranes of the superior nasal meatus. Which opening of the paranasal sinuses is most likely plugged?
questions.explanation: C (posterior ethmoidal sinus) — It opens into superior meatus; middle meatus receives anterior/middle ethmoid, maxillary and frontal drainage.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 53-year-old man has difficulty with breathing through his nose. On examination, his physician finds that he has swelling of the mucous membranes of the superior nasal meatus. Which opening of the paranasal sinuses is most likely plugged?

questions.question: A 5-year-old male child presents in the pediatric outpatient clinic with a complaint of difficulty in breathing through my nose for 7-days. He was breathing through the mouth. Oral examination revealed an enlarged mass in the nasopharynx. Enlargement of which of the following structures has most likely caused this condition?
questions.explanation: A (pharyngeal tonsil) — Adenoid enlargement obstructs nasopharynx; Eustachian tube, uvula, lingual tonsil and glands are not the typical midline mass.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 5-year-old male child presents in the pediatric outpatient clinic with a complaint of difficulty in breathing through my nose for 7-days. He was breathing through the mouth. Oral examination revealed an enlarged mass in the nasopharynx. Enlargement of which of the following structures has most likely caused this condition?

questions.question: A child had difficulty breathing due to an enlarged mass in the nasopharynx, what is the source of the obstruction?
questions.explanation: A (pharyngeal tonsil) — Adenoids in roof/posterior wall of nasopharynx cause nasal obstruction; lingual tonsil and sinuses are not there.
questions.sourceQuestion: A child had difficulty breathing due to an enlarged mass in the nasopharynx, what is the source of the obstruction?

questions.question: Where is Renkie's space? (Not included in 19th batch curriculum)
questions.explanation: B (vocal folds) — Reinke space is superficial lamina propria of true vocal fold; vocalis muscle, ventricle, and epiglottis are not the space itself. Marked “not included” in booklet curriculum.
questions.sourceQuestion: Where is Renkie's space? (Not included in 19th batch curriculum)

questions.question: Which of the following nerves is responsible for supplying the diaphragm?
questions.explanation: A (phrenic nerve) — Motor supply to diaphragm is phrenic C3–C5; vagus/recurrent/cardiopulmonary are not motor supply, intercostals supply peripheral sensory portions.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following nerves is responsible for supplying the diaphragm?

questions.question: When the intercostal muscles contract, the middle of the ribs is raised in what is known as the “bucket handle” movement. What is the effect of this movement on the thoracic cavity?
options: Decrease in the transverse dimension of the thorax
Increase in the transverse dimension of the thorax
Increase in the AP dimension of the thorax
Decrease in the AP dimension of the thorax
Increase in the vertical dimension of the thorax
questions.explanation: B (increased transverse dimension) — Bucket-handle rib movement increases transverse diameter; AP/vertical choices describe pump-handle or diaphragmatic movement.
questions.sourceQuestion: When the intercostal muscles contract, the middle of the ribs is raised in what is known as the “bucket handle” movement. What is the effect of this movement on the thoracic cavity?

questions.question: A 55-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital with a cough and severe dyspnea. Radiographic examination reveals that the patient suffers from emphysema. Upon physical examination the patient shows only "bucket handle movements" during deep inspiration. Which of the following movements of the thoracic wall is characteristic for this type of breathing?
options: Increase of the transverse diameter of the thorax
Increase of the anteroposterior diameter of the thorax
Increase of the vertical dimension of the thorax
Decrease of the anteroposterior diameter of the thorax
Decrease of the transverse diameter of the thorax
questions.explanation: A (transverse diameter increases) — Bucket-handle motion raises mid-ribs laterally; AP and vertical options describe different motions or wrong direction.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 55-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital with a cough and severe dyspnea. Radiographic examination reveals that the patient suffers from emphysema. Upon physical examination the patient shows only "bucket handle movements" during deep inspiration. Which of the following movements of the thoracic wall is characteristic for this type of breathing?

questions.question: What nerve plays a crucial role in the innervation of the diaphragm, and its damage can lead to diaphragmatic paralysis?
questions.explanation: C (phrenic C3–C5) — It provides diaphragm motor innervation; other nerves listed do not.
questions.sourceQuestion: What nerve plays a crucial role in the innervation of the diaphragm, and its damage can lead to diaphragmatic paralysis?

questions.question: What is the correct order of structures in the intercostal groove from superior to inferior?
questions.explanation: C (vein, artery, nerve) — VAN lies superior-to-inferior in costal groove; alternatives reverse the usual order.
questions.sourceQuestion: What is the correct order of structures in the intercostal groove from superior to inferior?

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary muscle for quiet inspiration?
questions.explanation: C (diaphragm) — Principal quiet inspiratory muscle; external intercostals assist, internal/innermost are mainly forced expiration/intercostal support.
questions.sourceQuestion: Which of the following is the primary muscle for quiet inspiration?

questions.question: What happens in a quiet respiration?
questions.explanation: C (diaphragm flattens) — Contraction descends/flattens diaphragm, increasing thoracic vertical dimension; A not always, B is false because AP does not decrease.
questions.sourceQuestion: What happens in a quiet respiration?

questions.question: If there are multiple fractures on 6 ribs due to an accident, how would these ribs move during inspiration?
options: Opposite to chest wall during inspiration
Same direction as chest wall during inspiration
questions.explanation: A (move opposite to chest wall) — Flail segment is pulled inward during inspiration as intact thorax expands; same-direction motion is normal chest wall.
questions.sourceIssue: The source recalls only 2 choices; preserved verbatim.
questions.sourceQuestion: If there are multiple fractures on 6 ribs due to an accident, how would these ribs move during inspiration?

questions.question: A patient has pneumonia and feels severe pain in their lateral chest wall, which nerve when blocked will relieve her pain?
questions.explanation: B (intercostal nerve) — Lateral thoracic wall pain travels in intercostal nerves; phrenic carries central diaphragm/pleural referred pain, vagus/splanchnic are not somatic chest wall afferents.
questions.sourceQuestion: A patient has pneumonia and feels severe pain in their lateral chest wall, which nerve when blocked will relieve her pain?

questions.question: Diaphragm is supplied by both phrenic and intercostal nerves. What may be the reason for an innervation of diaphragm by the intercostal nerve?
options: Diaphragm is close to lower intercostal muscles
Central tendon of diaphragm is a part of intercostal muscles
Pleuroperitoneal membrane is derived from intercostal muscles
A part of diaphragm is developed from lateral body wall muscles
questions.explanation: D (diaphragm partly derived from body-wall muscle) — Peripheral muscular diaphragm grows from body wall and receives lower intercostal innervation; other embryologic claims are incorrect.
questions.sourceQuestion: Diaphragm is supplied by both phrenic and intercostal nerves. What may be the reason for an innervation of diaphragm by the intercostal nerve?

questions.question: A 25-year-old woman is admitted to hospital with dyspnea. Radiologic examination reveals a tumor invading the lung surface just anterior to the hilum. Which nerve is being compressed by the tumor?
questions.explanation: A (phrenic nerve) — It runs anterior to lung root and is vulnerable to anterior hilar tumor; vagus passes posterior to root, others are not adjacent.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 25-year-old woman is admitted to hospital with dyspnea. Radiologic examination reveals a tumor invading the lung surface just anterior to the hilum. Which nerve is being compressed by the tumor?

questions.question: A patient was present with a defective bucket handle movement during inspiration , which of the following mechanisms explains the bucket-handle mechanism?
options: An increase in the transverse diameter of the thorax
An increase in the anterior-posterior diameter of the thorax
A decrease in the transverse diameter of the thorax
A decrease in the anterior-posterior diameter of the thorax
An increase in the vertical diameter of the thorax
questions.explanation: A (increased transverse diameter) — Bucket-handle increases transverse width; AP/vertical alternatives are not its action.
questions.sourceQuestion: A patient was present with a defective bucket handle movement during inspiration , which of the following mechanisms explains the bucket-handle mechanism?

questions.question: When the intercostal muscles contract, the middle of the ribs is raised in what is known as the “pump-handle” movement. What is the effect of this movement on the thoracic cavity?
options: Decrease in the transverse dimension of the thorax
Increase in the transverse dimension of the thorax
Increase in the anteroposterior dimension of the thorax
Decrease in the anteroposterior dimension of the thorax
Increase in the vertical dimension of the thorax
questions.explanation: C (increased AP dimension) — Pump-handle elevates sternum and increases AP diameter; transverse is bucket-handle, other choices wrong direction/axis.
questions.sourceQuestion: When the intercostal muscles contract, the middle of the ribs is raised in what is known as the “pump-handle” movement. What is the effect of this movement on the thoracic cavity?

questions.question: A 57-year-old man got hit by a truck and came in with broken ribs. Upon inspiration and expiration, he felt pain in his chest. Which nerve conducts this pain?
questions.explanation: D (intercostal nerves) — Rib and intercostal-space pain is carried by intercostal nerves; vagus/recurrent/splanchnic do not supply chest wall somatic sensation.
questions.sourceQuestion: A 57-year-old man got hit by a truck and came in with broken ribs. Upon inspiration and expiration, he felt pain in his chest. Which nerve conducts this pain?

questions.question: A man presented to the doctors office with ptosis, drooping of eyelids, and hemianhidrosis. He was diagnosed with a pancoast tumor, compression of which of the following best explains his previously mentioned symptoms?
questions.explanation: B (sympathetic trunk) — Pancoast tumor can interrupt cervical sympathetic pathway causing Horner syndrome; vagus, recurrent laryngeal and phrenic do not explain ptosis/anhidrosis.
questions.sourceQuestion: A man presented to the doctors office with ptosis, drooping of eyelids, and hemianhidrosis. He was diagnosed with a pancoast tumor, compression of which of the following best explains his previously mentioned symptoms?

questions.question: A person gets something stuck in his airways while swallowing, where is it most likely found?
questions.explanation: A (right main bronchus) — More vertical, wider and shorter than left, so aspirates favor it; all left options are less likely.
questions.sourceQuestion: A person gets something stuck in his airways while swallowing, where is it most likely found?

questions.question: A surgeon cut the segmental bronchus supplying the right superior lobe of the lung. Which bronchopulmonary segments are affected?
options: Superior, Anterior Basal, posterior basal, lateral basal, lateral medial
questions.explanation: B (posterior, anterior, apical segments) — Right upper lobe has apical, posterior, anterior segments; other options are middle/lower lobe or lingular segments.
questions.sourceQuestion: A surgeon cut the segmental bronchus supplying the right superior lobe of the lung. Which bronchopulmonary segments are affected?

questions.question: A child swallowed one of the wheels while playing with his toy cars. Which part of the conducting system is the wheel most likely stuck in?
questions.explanation: A (right main bronchus) — Same aspiration anatomy; left lobar branches and carina are less common locations.
questions.sourceQuestion: A child swallowed one of the wheels while playing with his toy cars. Which part of the conducting system is the wheel most likely stuck in?

questions.question: Patient comes in with chest pain. Scan reveals bronchogenic carcinoma growing anterior to the hilum of the lung. Which of the following is most likely compressed?
questions.explanation: A (phrenic nerve) — Phrenic passes anterior to lung root; vagus posterior, intercostal and sympathetic trunk are not at anterior hilum.
questions.sourceQuestion: Patient comes in with chest pain. Scan reveals bronchogenic carcinoma growing anterior to the hilum of the lung. Which of the following is most likely compressed?

questions.question: If there is a tumor above the horizontal fissure, which lobe will be affected?
questions.explanation: C (right superior lobe) — Right horizontal fissure separates upper from middle lobe; left has no horizontal fissure, lower lobe is below oblique fissure.
questions.sourceQuestion: If there is a tumor above the horizontal fissure, which lobe will be affected?

questions.question: During physical examination, the medical resident identifies the point where the trachea bifurcates into the right and left main bronchi. This anatomical landmark is known as:
