questions.sourceExplanation: A = head, B = neck, C = tubercle, D = scalene tubercle, E = vessel grooves, F = costal cartilage. This broad flat rib is atypical. The other atypical ribs are 2 and 10–12. Subclavian vein lies anterior and artery posterior to the scalene tubercle.

questions.question:
A) Identify and name A, B, C, D, E, F
B) What type of Vertebra is this?
C) Where are they present?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) A- Body
B- Superior Demi facet
C- Pedicle
D- Transverse Process
E- Lamina
F- Spinous Process
G- Foramen
B) Thoracic Vertebrae
C) T2-T9
questions.sourceExplanation: A = body, B = superior costal demifacet, C = pedicle, D = transverse process, E = lamina, F = spinous process, G = vertebral foramen. The rib facets identify thoracic anatomy. T2–T9 is the intended typical range, with variation in lower thoracic facets.

questions.question:
A) Identify and name A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H
B) What type of Vertebra is this?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) A- Superior Articular Process
B- Transverse Process
C- Transverse Foramen
D- Body
E- Groove for spinal nerve
F- Pedicle
G- Spinous process
H- Vertebral Foramen
I- Lamina
B) Cervical Vertebra
A Identify and name A, B, C, D, E, F
questions.sourceExplanation: A = superior articular process, B = transverse process, C = transverse foramen, D = body, E = spinal nerve groove, F = pedicle, G = spinous process, H = vertebral foramen, I = lamina. Transverse foramina and a bifid spine distinguish this typical cervical specimen.

questions.question:
A) Identify and name A, B, C, D, E, F
B) What type of vertebra is this?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) A- Body
B- Pedicle
C- Superior Articular Process
D- Superior Articular Facet
E- Spinous Process
F- Transverse Process
B) Lumbar Vertebra
questions.sourceExplanation: A = body, B = pedicle, C = superior articular process, D = its superior articular facet, E = spinous process, F = transverse process. The broad body and stout spinous process fit a lumbar vertebra, without rib facets or transverse foramina.

questions.question:
A) Identify the structure labeled with the red arrow
B) What openings does it has?
questions.printedAnswer:
A. Superior meatus
B. Opening of the posterior ethmoidal sinus
questions.sourceExplanation: Below the superior concha. It receives posterior ethmoidal air cells. The sphenoid opens into the recess above the superior concha.

questions.question:
A) Identify the structure labeled with the red arrow
B) What openings does it has?
questions.printedAnswer:
A. Ethmoidal bulla
B. Opening of the middle ethmoidal sinus
questions.sourceExplanation: The bulge in the middle meatus is formed by middle ethmoidal cells, whose ostia commonly open on its surface or just above it.

questions.question:
A) Identify the structure labeled with the red arrow
B) What openings does it has?
questions.printedAnswer:
A. Inferior meatus
B. Opening of the nasolacrimal duct
questions.sourceExplanation: The channel below the inferior concha receives the nasolacrimal duct.

questions.question:
A) Which between A & B are the true/false vocal cords
B) Identify the structure labeled with the blue arrow
questions.printedAnswer:
A) A: false vocal cords B: true vocal cords
B) Cricoid cartilage
questions.sourceExplanation: A is the superior vestibular or false fold. B is the lower true vocal fold. The blue arrow marks the complete ring of cricoid cartilage below the folds.

questions.question:
A) Identify the muscle labeled with the red arrow
B) What is the nerve supply for this muscle?
questions.printedAnswer:
A. Cricothyroid
B. Superior laryngeal nerve
questions.sourceExplanation: This anterior muscle tilts thyroid cartilage relative to the cricoid and stretches the vocal folds. Its motor supply is specifically the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve.

questions.question: What is the function of the thymus gland and where is it exactly located?
questions.printedAnswer:
The thymus gland is located in the anterior mediastinum of the inferior mediastinum. It is the site at which
immature lymphocytes develop into T-lymphocytes and secrete thymic hormones which cause T-lymphocytes
to gain immunocompetence)
extra points: it begins involution after puberty
questions.sourceExplanation: It lies behind the sternum in the superior and adjacent anterior mediastinal region. It supports T-cell maturation and selection and involutes with age. Incomplete location in key: it can extend superiorly toward the neck, particularly in children. Pediatric mediastinal imaging (https://doi.org/10.37549/ar2428)

questions.question: Which of the following 2 bones make up the inferior thoracic outlet?
questions.sourceExplanation: The intended specimens are 1, the lower thoracic vertebra (T12), and 6, a lower rib. The full boundary includes T12, ribs 11 and 12, costal margins and the xiphisternal joint. Labels 2/5/7 belong to the superior aperture and the isolated body of the sternum does not form the lower boundary.

questions.question: Which structure will probably get obstructed by inhaled food, X (23) or Y (24)?
questions.sourceExplanation: Y (24) — Right bronchus. The right main bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical. X is the left-sided bronchial option, which is more oblique.

questions.question:
A) Label structure X
B) Mention 2 nerves supplying it
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Inferior vena cava
B) Phrenic nerve and intercostal nerve
questions.sourceExplanation: Diaphragm model. Wording mismatch. X indicates IVC at the caval opening. The two nerves in the printed answer refer to diaphragmatic innervation (the surrounding structure Y). Phrenic nerves supply diaphragm motor fibres and central sensation. Lower intercostal nerves carry peripheral sensation.

questions.question:
A) Name X
B) What sound does this make?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) The mitral/bicuspid valve
B) The first heart sound, S1, “Lubb”
questions.sourceExplanation: X is the left AV valve. Its closure contributes to S1 at the start of systole.

questions.question:
A) Label the marked structure
B) Give 2 arteries that supply it
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Interventricular septum
B) Left anterior descending (anterior ⅓) and posterior interventricular artery (posterior ⅔)
questions.sourceExplanation: Interventricular septum. Incorrect key fractions. LAD septal branches supply the anterior two-thirds and the posterior interventricular artery supplies the posterior one-third in the standard description. The key reverses the fractions. The artery giving the posterior interventricular branch depends on coronary dominance.

questions.question:
A) Name the structure
B) How does it develop?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Coronary sinus
B) from the left horn of sinus venosus
questions.sourceExplanation: This large vessel runs in the posterior AV groove and drains cardiac veins into the RA. It develops from the left horn of the sinus venosus.

questions.question:
A) Identify the structures numbered 32 and 33
B) How is 33 formed?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) 32: Ascending aorta, 33: Superior vena cava
B) Right and left brachiocephalic veins
questions.sourceExplanation: 32 is the ascending aorta; 33 sits to its right and is the SVC, formed by union of the right and left brachiocephalic veins.

questions.question:
A) Name the structure marked by the arrow
B) Give a clinical condition where the circled area is obliterated
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Trachea
B) Pleural effusion, ex: hemothorax
questions.sourceExplanation: The arrow points to tracheal air. A pleural effusion can blunt the circled costophrenic angle. A hemothorax is one cause of pleural fluid.

questions.question: Name the artery marked by the red arrow
questions.sourceExplanation: The keyed arrow identifies LAD. Its course and small septal branches help distinguish it from circumflex and its marginal branches. Angiographic orientation varies with projection.

questions.question: What is this vessel?
questions.sourceExplanation: Angiogram. Suspect key. The booklet calls the vessel circumflex. The arrow appears to point near a side-branch takeoff from the vessel marked LAD, with a nearby diagonal label. A diagonal branch or its LAD junction is more plausible. The small image does not allow a confident exact segment label.

questions.question: Put the pin on the trachea
questions.sourceExplanation: Pin 14, the central air-filled lumen anterior to the oesophagus.

questions.question: Put the pin on the thoracic aorta
questions.sourceExplanation: Pin 21, the descending aorta beside the vertebral body on the patient’s left.

questions.question: Put the pin on the left atrium
questions.sourceExplanation: Pin 28, the posterior chamber anterior to the oesophagus, where the pulmonary veins enter.

questions.question: What are these X and Y?
questions.printedAnswer:
X: Inferior vena cava
Y: Aorta
questions.sourceExplanation: X is IVC in the central tendon (T8). Y is aorta at the posterior hiatus (T12).

questions.question: Which one shows hemothorax on the xray
questions.sourceExplanation: A — Pleural fluid. A has a basal opacity and meniscus compatible with pleural fluid. B shows the pleural line and peripheral loss of markings of pneumothorax. Qualification: a plain film can show fluid, but confirming that it is blood needs context or further evaluation.

questions.question: Which ones form the upper thoracic outlet?
questions.sourceExplanation: 2, 5 and 7 are the T1 vertebra, manubrium and first rib specimen. The complete boundary uses both first ribs and their cartilages. The other bones shown are outside the aperture.

questions.question: What nerve supplied the muscle labelled X?
questions.sourceExplanation: X is the posterior cricoarytenoid, which abducts the vocal folds. Its motor supply is the recurrent laryngeal nerve via its inferior laryngeal continuation.

questions.question: What abnormalities can be seen in the following X-rays:
questions.sourceExplanation: A suggests a pneumothorax from peripheral absent lung markings. B shows dependent pleural opacity consistent with fluid. The keyed hemothorax requires the appropriate clinical context.

questions.question: Name the vessel where X drains and mention the level:
questions.sourceExplanation: X is the azygos system on the right of the vertebral column, arching to join the SVC around T4 (near the sternal angle plane).

questions.question:
Which of the given bones marked as 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 and 8 make the boundary of
superior thoracic aperture?
questions.sourceExplanation: 2 (T1), 5 (manubrium) and 7 (first rib). These form the posterior, anterior and lateral borders respectively, with the first costal cartilages completing the sides.

questions.question:
A 45-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital with severe dyspnea. Physical
examination reveals the patient has miosis of the pupil, partial ptosis of the eyelid,
and anhidrosis of the face. Her X-Ray is attached. Name the structure responsible
for this condition:
questions.sourceExplanation: The apical lesion can compress the ipsilateral sympathetic trunk, accounting for miosis, mild ptosis and anhidrosis.

questions.question: Identify the structures: 20, 17, 39, 12
questions.printedAnswer:
20-left brachiocephalic vein
17-right brachiocephalic vein
12-left subclavian artery
39-2nd/3rd Thoracic Vertebrae
questions.sourceExplanation: 20 marks left brachiocephalic vein, which crosses the upper mediastinum. 17 marks right brachiocephalic vein. 12 is left subclavian artery, a lateral arch branch. 39 is the upper thoracic vertebral body, labelled T2/T3 in the key. Exact level needs serial imaging or additional landmarks.

questions.question:
A)Mention the specific name of the anatomical feature at which the red arrow is pointing at, also mention its
vertebral level.
B) Provide an example where it is clinically (pathologically) involved.
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Carina at T4/5
B) Tracheobronchial nodes cancer
questions.sourceExplanation: This is the ridge where trachea bifurcates, near T4–T5 at the sternal-angle plane. Enlarged subcarinal/tracheobronchial nodes, for example from malignancy, can widen or distort the carinal angle.

questions.question: What makes the right border of the heart?
questions.printedAnswer:
1) Right atrium
2) Superior vena cava
3) Inferior Vena cava
questions.sourceExplanation: The right atrium forms most of the right cardiac silhouette on PA radiograph. The SVC contributes to the upper right mediastinal silhouette, and the IVC may contribute to the lower cavoatrial contour. If the examiner asks for the anatomical heart border alone, answer right atrium.

questions.question:
A) Identify the structure B
B)What is the outcome if structure A is stimulated
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Accessory hemiazygos
B) Diaphragm contraction and referred pain at C3-C5 in the shoulder region
questions.sourceExplanation: B is accessory hemiazygos, descending on the left in the upper posterior thorax. A is the phrenic nerve. Motor stimulation contracts the ipsilateral hemidiaphragm. Irritation of the nerve’s central diaphragmatic sensory territory can refer pain to the shoulder via C3–C5.

questions.question: Which of the given bones marked as 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 and 8 make the boundary of superior thoracic aperture?
questions.sourceExplanation: Pins 2, 5 and 7 represent T1, the manubrium and the first rib. The complete boundary includes both first ribs and their cartilages.

questions.question:
A patient presented with difficulty swallowing, her case history revealed she had mitral valve
stenosis. Ultrasound showed the enlargement of one of the structures. Which of the following
chambers marked as W,X,Y and Z is responsible for this pain
questions.sourceExplanation: Z — Left atrium. Mitral stenosis raises LA pressure and can enlarge the chamber against the oesophagus. W and X lie on the right side of the echo. Y is the thick-walled LV, farther from the oesophagus than the LA.

questions.question:
A) Identify the marked structure with the red arrow
B) Which structure drains into the space immediately inferior to it?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Inferior concha
B) Nasolacrimal duct drains into the inferior meatus
questions.sourceExplanation: The inferior nasal concha is the lowest turbinate on the lateral nasal wall; the inferior meatus lies directly below it. The nasolacrimal duct drains into that meatus.

questions.question:
A) Name the structure indicated by the arrow
B) Name the artery supplying it
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Fibrous pericardium
B) Pericardiacophrenic artery
questions.sourceExplanation: The arrow marks the fibrous pericardium, the tough outer sac around the heart. The pericardiacophrenic artery, a branch of the internal thoracic artery, supplies it while accompanying the phrenic nerve.

questions.question:
A) Identify whether this is the right lung or left lung
B) Name two identification features
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Left lung
B) 1 oblique fissure (no horizontal fissure) / only two lobes/lingula/cardiac notch
questions.sourceExplanation: This is the left lung: it has one oblique fissure and lacks a horizontal fissure. The cardiac notch and lingula are additional left-sided features.

questions.question:
A) What nerve is marked with the arrow?
B) How does impairing this nerve affect your respiratory function?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Left Phrenic nerve
B) Paradoxical movement of the diaphragm
questions.sourceExplanation: The left phrenic nerve descends on the fibrous pericardium to the diaphragm. Injury weakens or paralyzes the ipsilateral hemidiaphragm, reducing inspiration and potentially causing paradoxical upward movement during inspiration.

questions.question:
A) What is the name of the structure labelled X?
B) What would happen if the structure labelled Y was damaged?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Papillary muscles (specifically the septal one)
B) Tricuspid valve regurgitation due to cusp prolapse upon ventricular systole
questions.sourceExplanation: X is the septal papillary muscle of the right ventricle; its chordae attach to tricuspid cusps. Damage to Y, the chordal-papillary support, can let a cusp prolapse during systole and cause tricuspid regurgitation.

questions.question:
A) Identify structure A.
B) Explain what will happen if B is damaged.
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Chordae tendineae
B) A V valve will not close, causing backflow of blood into the atrium.
questions.sourceExplanation: Chordae tendineae connect AV valve cusps to papillary muscles and prevent cusp eversion during systole. Papillary muscle injury can loosen this restraint and cause regurgitation; the valve may still partly close, so ‘will not close’ is too absolute.

questions.question:
A) What is the name of the cavity below this structure?
B) Name two air sinuses that drain into it.
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Middle meatus
B) Frontal and maxillary sinuses.
questions.sourceExplanation: The middle meatus lies below the middle nasal concha. The frontal and maxillary sinuses drain there, along with anterior and middle ethmoidal cells.

questions.question:
A) Name the structure that causes the impression at A, be specific with your answer.
B) Name the structure point at B.
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Arch of aorta
B) Left primary bronchus
questions.sourceExplanation: The arch of the aorta makes the superior aortic impression on the left lung. The lower marked structure at the hilum is the left main bronchus.

questions.question:
A) Name the artery which supplies blood to the structure indicated by the arrow.
B) Name one clinical condition associated with this.
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Pericardiophrenic of the internal thoracic artery
B) Pericarditis/ Cardiac tamponade
questions.sourceExplanation: The pericardiacophrenic artery branches from the internal thoracic artery and accompanies the phrenic nerve along the pericardium. Pericarditis or cardiac tamponade involves the pericardium, though the artery is not a diagnostic marker for either condition.

questions.question:
A) What is the MAJOR nerve supplying this structure
B) Name TWO embryological origins of this structure
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Phrenic Nerve
B) Septum transversum, mesentery of esophagus, pleuroperitoneal membrane
questions.sourceExplanation: The phrenic nerve (C3–C5) is the diaphragm’s principal motor supply. The diaphragm develops from the septum transversum, pleuroperitoneal membranes, dorsal mesentery of the esophagus, and muscular ingrowth from the body wall; any two are acceptable.

questions.question:
A) Which pericardial sinus is the surgical instrument going through?
B) What two structures are anterior to it?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Transverse sinus
B) Aorta & Pulmonary Trunk
questions.sourceExplanation: The instrument passes through the transverse pericardial sinus, behind the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk and in front of the SVC. The aorta and pulmonary trunk lie anterior to the sinus.

questions.question:
A) Which lung is it?
B) 2 characteristics to justify your answer
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Right lung
B) Horizontal fissure & Middle lobe
questions.sourceExplanation: This is the right lung, identified by its horizontal fissure and middle lobe. The left lung has no horizontal fissure and instead has a cardiac notch and lingula.

questions.question:
A) What is X and Y
B) What is the function of Y?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) X is Chordae Tendineae & Y is Papillary muscle
B) Stabilizes the cusps
A) Function of X
questions.sourceExplanation: X is chordae tendineae and Y is a papillary muscle. During systole, papillary muscle contraction tensions the chordae to prevent AV cusp prolapse; it does not open the valve.

questions.question:
A) Function of X
B) Which nerve supplies X?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Abduction of vocal cords
B) Recurrent laryngeal nerve
questions.sourceExplanation: X is the posterior cricoarytenoid, the only intrinsic laryngeal muscle that abducts the vocal folds. It is supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve; the printed key gives the action and nerve but omits the requested muscle identification.

questions.question: In case of a Stab wound injury to the heart, which chamber is most likely to be injured?
questions.sourceExplanation: The right ventricle is the most anterior heart chamber and is the expected answer for a generic anterior stab wound. The printed key says left ventricle, but the stem gives no wound location or trajectory, so the specific chamber is not strictly determined.

questions.question:
A) Identify structures A and B
B) What two structures form structure A
questions.printedAnswer:
A) A: Right brachiocephalic vein. B: Left brachiocephalic vein
B) Right jugular vein and right subclavian vein
questions.sourceExplanation: A is the right brachiocephalic vein and B the left brachiocephalic vein; they join to form the SVC. The right brachiocephalic vein forms from the right internal jugular and right subclavian veins.

questions.question:
A) Name the coronary artery highlighted by the arrow with the letter A
B) State what it supplies
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Left anterior descending artery
B) It supplies two thirds of the interventricular septum and the bundle of His
questions.sourceExplanation: The LAD descends in the anterior interventricular groove and supplies the anterior wall and apex of the left ventricle and most of the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum. The printed claim that it supplies the bundle of His is too broad; His bundle supply varies.

questions.question:
A) Identify whether this is the right lung or left lung
B) Name two identification features
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Left lung
B) Oblique fissure but no horizontal fissure, presence of lingula
questions.sourceExplanation: This is the left lung: it has one oblique fissure, a cardiac notch, and a lingula, and lacks the right lung’s horizontal fissure and middle lobe.

questions.question:
A) Name structure A
B) Name the function of structure A
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Moderator band (septomarginal band)
B) Contains right bundle branch and conducts action potential, ensuring that the right ventricle contracts at the
same time as the left ventricle
questions.sourceExplanation: The moderator band (septomarginal trabecula) crosses the right ventricle and carries the right bundle branch toward the anterior papillary muscle, helping coordinate right ventricular activation. It does not carry the left bundle branch.

questions.question:
A)What is the name of the artery (indicated by the red arrow)
B) What part of the heart does it supply?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Left anterior descending (LAD)
B)It supplies the majority (usually two-thirds or more) of the interventricula
septum (the anterior part).
questions.sourceExplanation: The LAD runs in the anterior interventricular sulcus and supplies adjacent left ventricular myocardium and most of the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum.

questions.question:
A) Name the branch indicated by the red arrow, and mention the part of the heart
that is supplies
B) Name the vessel (indicated by the green arrow)
questions.printedAnswer:
A)Posterior interventricular artery (PIA), it supplies the posterior part of the interventricular septum (1/3) but
not apically
B)Middle cardiac vein
questions.sourceExplanation: The posterior interventricular artery runs in the posterior interventricular sulcus and supplies the posterior third of the septum and adjacent ventricular walls. Its territory varies with coronary dominance, so ‘but not apically’ is an oversimplification. The accompanying vein is the middle cardiac vein.

questions.question: Name the vessel (indicated by the red arrow)
questions.sourceExplanation: The great cardiac vein accompanies the LAD in the anterior interventricular groove before turning into the coronary sulcus.

questions.question:
A) What sinus of the heart is shown?
B) Name the vessel(s) anterior to the opening of the sinus.
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Transverse sinus
B) Ascending aorta and/ or pulmonary trunk
questions.sourceExplanation: The transverse pericardial sinus lies behind the arterial outflow tracts and in front of the SVC. The ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk are anterior to it.

questions.question:
A) Which pin (red or blue) represents the nerve that supplies the visceral
pericardium?
B) Name two structures suppled by the nerve pinned blue.
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Red pin (visceral is supplied by vagus nerve)
B) Parietal and fibrous pericardium, and the diaphragm
questions.sourceExplanation: The red pin marks the vagus, which contributes autonomic fibers to the cardiac plexus and visceral pericardium; sympathetic cardiac branches also contribute. The blue pin marks the phrenic nerve, which supplies the diaphragm motorically and the fibrous and parietal serous pericardium sensorially.

questions.question:
A) Which of the two lungs is displayed on the image?
B) Name structure A
C) Name structure B
D) Name structure C
E) Which surface of the lung is displayed on the image to right?
F) Name the other surfaces of the lung
questions.printedAnswer:
A) The left lung
B) Pulmonary artery
C) Bronchi
D) Pulmonary vein (NOTE: Use the abbreviation ABV to remember the order of the structures in the hilum of
the LEFT lung)
E) The mediastinal surface
F) Costal surface and Diaphragmatic surface
questions.sourceExplanation: This is the left lung on its mediastinal surface. At the hilum, A is pulmonary artery, B bronchus, and C pulmonary vein; on the left the artery is superior to the bronchus (ABV). The other surfaces are costal and diaphragmatic.

questions.question:
A) Which of the two lungs is displayed on the image on the right?
B) Name structure A
C) Name structure B
D) Name structure C
questions.printedAnswer:
A) The Right lung
B)Bronchi
C) Pulmonary Artery
D)Pulmonary Vein (NOTE: use the abbreviation BAV to remember the order of the structures in the hilum of
the RIGHT lung)
questions.sourceExplanation: This is the right lung. At its hilum A is bronchus, B pulmonary artery, and C pulmonary vein; on the right the artery lies anterior to the bronchus (BAV).

questions.question:
A) Name the organ that caused impression A
B) Name the organ that caused impression B
C) Name the organ that caused impression C
D) Name the organ that caused impression D
E) Name the organ that caused impression E
F) Name the organ that caused impression F
G) Name structure G
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Arch of azygous vein
B)Esophagus
C)Brachiocephalic vein
D) Superior vena cava
E) The heart
F)Inferior vena cava
G)Pulmonary ligament
questions.sourceExplanation: The right lung impressions are A azygos arch, B esophagus, C right brachiocephalic vein, D SVC, E heart, and F IVC. G is the pulmonary ligament, a pleural fold extending below the root. These are not all ‘organs,’ as the stem loosely calls them.

questions.question:
A) Name the organ that caused impression A
B) Name the organ that caused impression B
C) Name the organ that caused impression C
D) Name the organ that caused impression D
questions.printedAnswer:
A)Arch of aorta
B) Descending aorta
C)Left subclavian artery
D)The heart
questions.sourceExplanation: On the left lung, A is the aortic arch, B the descending thoracic aorta, C the left subclavian artery, and D the heart. The azygos arch and IVC impressions are on the right lung.

questions.question:
A) list down the contents of the middle mediastinum:
B) list down the contents of the posterior mediastinum:
C) name the structure covered in red and state its function:
questions.printedAnswer:
A)
● Heart within the pericardium
● Roots of great vessels ( aorta, pulmonary arteries and veins, SVC, IVC)
● Phrenic nerve
● Main bronchi
● Arch of the azygous vein
B)
● Esophagus (with vagal plexuses)
● Descending aorta and branches
● Azygos and Hemiazygos venous systems
● Thoracic duct
● Sympathetic trunk and splanchnic nerves
C) Phrenic nerve function: The phrenic nerves provide motor innervation to the diaphragm and work in
conjunction with secondary respirator muscles (trapezius, pectoralis major, pectoralis minor,
sternocleidomastoid, and intercostals) to allow respiration.
questions.sourceExplanation: The middle mediastinum contains the heart and pericardium, intrapericardial parts of the great vessels, main bronchi, phrenic nerves, and pericardiacophrenic vessels. The azygos arch is usually classified in the superior mediastinum. The posterior mediastinum contains the esophagus and vagal plexus, descending thoracic aorta, azygos system, thoracic duct, sympathetic trunks, and thoracic splanchnic nerves. The red structure is the azygos vein, which drains the posterior thoracic wall to the SVC; the printed key calls it the phrenic nerve, which is incorrect because the phrenic descends on the pericardium.

questions.question: Name the structures covered in blue (A, B and C) and their location in mediastinum
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Thoracic sympathetic trunk, located in the posterior mediastinum
B) Azygous vein, located in the middle mediastinum
C) Thoracic duct, located in the posterior mediastinum.
Refer to the attached image:
questions.sourceExplanation: A is the thoracic sympathetic trunk in the posterior mediastinum; B is the azygos vein, also in the posterior mediastinum; C is the thoracic duct in the posterior mediastinum. The printed placement of the main azygos vein in the middle mediastinum is incorrect; its arch is generally in the superior mediastinum.

questions.question:
A) Identify the structure marked by the arrow
B) Mention 2 effects that will happen after stimulation of this nerve
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Phrenic nerve
B) Contraction and relaxation of the diaphragm
questions.sourceExplanation: The arrow marks the phrenic nerve. Stimulation contracts the ipsilateral diaphragm and supports inspiration; relaxation follows when phrenic discharge ceases, rather than being a second direct effect of stimulation.

questions.question:
A) Name structure A
B) State the function of structure B
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Eustachian/auditory tube
B) Lingual tonsils: lymphatic organs that fight off infections
questions.sourceExplanation: A is the pharyngotympanic (auditory/Eustachian) tube connecting the nasopharynx and middle ear. B is the lingual tonsil, lymphoid tissue at the posterior tongue base that contributes to mucosal immune defense.

questions.question:
A) Name impressions X and Y
B) At what vertebral level does X drain into Y?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) X: arch of azygos vein, Y: superior vena cava.
B) X drains into Y at T4.
questions.sourceExplanation: X is the arch of the azygos vein and Y the SVC; the arch crosses over the right lung root to enter the SVC near the sternal-angle plane, approximately T4–T5. T4 is an accepted approximation, though the level varies.

questions.question:
Which one supplies the fibrous pericardium
Choose phrenic:
X
Put the pin on the arch of the aorta of this lung impression
questions.sourceExplanation: The phrenic nerve (X) supplies somatic sensory fibers to the fibrous and parietal pericardium; vagal fibers are autonomic. The aortic arch impression is the superior aortic impression on the left lung (pin X).

questions.question: Drag pin to the coronary sinus opening
questions.sourceExplanation: The coronary sinus opens into the right atrium near the IVC opening, posterior to the tricuspid orifice. Pin 6 matches the booklet image; confirm the tiny landmark against the original model if reusing this as a station.

questions.question:
Which of the following structures contribute to the formation of the cardiac
Plexus:
A) X
B) Y
questions.sourceExplanation: The cardiac plexus is formed by vagal cardiac branches and sympathetic cardiac nerves. X is a vagal cardiac branch; Y appears to mark the phrenic nerve, which supplies the diaphragm and pericardium rather than forming the plexus. The printed answer A is supported.

questions.question:
A patient presents with mitral valve stenosis, which of the following valves in the
echocardiographic image is involved:
A) A
B) B
questions.sourceExplanation: Mitral stenosis involves the left atrioventricular valve between the left atrium and ventricle; the marked valve is B. The tricuspid valve is right-sided.

questions.question: Identify structure labelled X:
questions.sourceExplanation: Chordae tendineae are fibrous strands connecting AV valve cusps to papillary muscles; they are distinct from both the cusps and the muscles.

questions.question: Name structures related to the marked areas
questions.sourceExplanation: The marked right lung impressions are the arch of the azygos vein and the esophagus. Corresponding left-sided impressions include the aortic arch and descending aorta.

questions.question: Determine the side of the lung and give two justification points
questions.sourceExplanation: The cardiac notch and lingula identify the left lung; it also has one oblique fissure and no horizontal fissure.

questions.question: Name the structures related to areas marked X and Y
questions.printedAnswer:
X) Superior vena cava or brachiocephalic vein depression
Y) Heart depression
questions.sourceExplanation: The primary bronchus enters the lung at the hilum and branches into lobar bronchi within the lung; the printed phrase ‘divides after going through the lungs’ is inaccurate. X marks the superior vena cava/brachiocephalic vein impression and Y the cardiac impression.

questions.question: Identify the structures marked as A,B and C
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Right coronary artery
B) right marginal artery or Ventricular Branches
C) left descending artery (LAD)
questions.sourceExplanation: A is the right coronary artery in the right AV groove; B is the right marginal artery (or a ventricular branch, depending on the arrow tip); C is the LAD in the anterior interventricular groove.

questions.question:
Which of the following (1,2,3,4) if stimulated will cause increased heart rate with normal ecg
components?
questions.sourceExplanation: Pin 3 marks the sinoatrial node region, the heart’s normal pacemaker. Stimulating it increases pacemaker firing and heart rate.

questions.question: Identify the structure and what is its main function?
questions.sourceExplanation: The arytenoid cartilage moves and anchors the vocal folds through its cricoarytenoid joint and muscle attachments, supporting phonation, breathing, and airway protection. Phonation is not its only function.

questions.question: Identify the structure marked as 1 and state its importance in fetal life
questions.printedAnswer:
Fossa ovalis , shunting blood between the right and left atrium
Physiology Lab
questions.sourceExplanation: Structure 1 is the fossa ovalis, the adult remnant of the fetal foramen ovale. In fetal life the foramen ovale shunts blood from right atrium to left atrium; the fossa ovalis itself is not the fetal shunt.

questions.question:
A) Calculate the heart rate of regions X and Y
B) What does the brown arrow show you?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) X: 300/3 =100 bpm, Y: 300/6 =50 bpm
B) It shows R-R interval resembling the duration of 1 cardiac cycle
questions.sourceExplanation: At 25 mm/s, heart rate is approximately 300 divided by the number of large boxes between R waves: X is about 3 boxes (100 bpm) and Y about 6 (50 bpm). The brown arrow marks an R–R interval, one beat’s ventricular cycle duration; rates are approximate.

questions.question:
A) What parameter is decreased in restrictive lung disease
B) Which one of the labelled graphs represents obstructive lung disease?
questions.sourceExplanation: Restriction reduces TLC and usually FVC and FEV₁; RV may be low or normal. The FEV₁/FVC ratio is generally preserved or increased, so the printed list is incomplete if read as saying the ratio falls. Graph B is obstructive, with a scooped expiratory limb; reduced TLC confirms restriction.

questions.question:
A) Explain the changes observed in stage 1.
B) Which stage (1, 2, 3, or 4) will the venous return increase?
questions.sourceExplanation: During Valsalva phase I, straining abruptly raises intrathoracic pressure and briefly raises arterial pressure by compressing the aorta; baroreceptor firing rises and heart rate may briefly fall. Venous return rebounds in phase IV after release, producing a pressure and cardiac output overshoot.

questions.question:
A) Which graph is indicative of a restrictive disease?
B) Which graph has normal lung compliance?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Graph C
B) Graph A
questions.sourceExplanation: Graph C is restrictive: FEV₁ and FVC fall proportionally while volume is reduced. Graph A is the normal loop. A forced expiratory loop does not directly measure compliance, so the wording ‘normal lung compliance’ is imprecise.

questions.question:
A) Calculate systolic pressure in phase 1 in valsalva maneuver
B) What changes in the heart rate can you see in phase 1 of the valsalva maneuver
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Systolic Pressure = approximately 160 mm Hg
B) Heart rate will decrease
questions.sourceExplanation: The phase-I systolic peak is approximately 160 mmHg on the plotted scale. Heart rate transiently decreases as the initial pressure rise activates baroreceptors; both readings are approximate from the small trace.

questions.question:
A) What is the phenomenon shown in the ECG?
B) Calculate the heart rate.
C) On which, X or Y , is parasympathetic stimulation acting upon more?
questions.printedAnswer:
A) Respiratory Sinus Arrhythmia (rhythm during inspiration and inhalation)
B) Y= 300÷5= 60, X= 300÷3= 100
C) Y
questions.sourceExplanation: This is respiratory sinus arrhythmia: sinus rate rises with inspiration and falls with expiration. Using 300 divided by large boxes, X is about 100 bpm and Y about 60 bpm. Parasympathetic influence is greater at Y, where the R–R interval is longer; the printed ‘inspiration and inhalation’ is redundant.

questions.question: Put the pin to the curve that shows obstruction
questions.sourceExplanation: Place the pin on B: the obstructive loop has reduced early expiratory flow, a scooped expiratory limb, and prolonged emptying. A is normal; C has reduced volumes with a relatively preserved shape, consistent with restriction.

questions.question:
The changes in blood pressure and heart rate during the Valsalva Maneuver are
given in the attached tracing. The heart rate in phase II is increased due to:
A) Activation of the sympathetic axis
B) Increased pressure around the heart
questions.sourceExplanation: Phase-II heart rate rises through baroreflex sympathetic activation and vagal withdrawal after reduced venous return lowers stroke volume, cardiac output, and arterial pressure. Increased thoracic pressure is the initiating mechanical event, not the direct chronotropic mechanism; answer A is best.

questions.question:
What happens to the baroreceptors during phase 2 of valsalva maneuver?
A) Activated
B) Inhibited
C) At rest
questions.sourceExplanation: In phase II, continued straining reduces venous return and arterial pressure, decreasing baroreceptor stretch and firing. Thus baroreceptors are functionally inhibited (B); activation better describes the phase-I pressure rise.

questions.question:
The following changes occur during respiration. What happens to the heart rate during
expiration?
A) Increased
B) Decreased
C) No change
questions.sourceExplanation: During expiration, greater vagal influence slows the sinus rate, so heart rate decreases (B). Inspiration has the reciprocal effect in respiratory sinus arrhythmia.
